title: Graphing Polynomials
summary: A polynomial's graph is set by its degree and leading coefficient (end behavior), its real zeros (x-intercepts), and the multiplicity of each zero (cross vs touch). Together these sketch the curve's overall shape.

degree.in_class: Sets the number of turns and end behavior.

leading coefficient.in_class: Its sign controls the end behavior.

end behavior.in_class: Determined by degree and leading coefficient.

multiplicity.plain: How many times a factor repeats.

cross vs touch.plain: How the graph meets the x-axis at a zero.

concept_sections.heading: End behavior
concept_sections.explanation: The degree and leading coefficient set the ends: even degree sends both ends the same way, odd degree opposite ways; a positive leading coefficient lifts the right end.
math_steps: Look at the leading coefficient's sign.

concept_sections.heading: Zeros and factors
concept_sections.explanation: Real zeros are x-intercepts, found by setting the factored polynomial to zero. Each factor $(x-a)$ gives a zero at $a$.

concept_sections.heading: Multiplicity
concept_sections.explanation: A zero's multiplicity (the power of its factor) tells how the graph behaves there: odd multiplicity crosses the axis, even multiplicity touches and turns back.

concept_sections.heading: Turning points
concept_sections.explanation: A degree-$n$ polynomial has at most $n-1$ turning points. Between consecutive zeros the graph must turn.
math_steps: Use this to shape the sketch.

concept_sections.heading: Putting it together
concept_sections.explanation: Combine end behavior, x-intercepts with their multiplicities, and the y-intercept to sketch the full curve.
math_steps: Draw the ends from end behavior.
